Aggregate.description: A "how many, by what" count over the dialog store, one dimension.

buckets.description: The buckets, largest first, ties broken by value for a stable answer.

distinct_values.description: How many distinct values the dimension took, before the cut.

group_by.description: The dimension the count grouped by, echoed verbatim.

other_count.description:
Total count in every bucket past the `top_n` cut, so the answer still
sums to `total_matched`.

total_matched.description: How many dialogs the filter admitted, across all buckets.

AggregateBucket.description:
One bucket of an aggregate: a grouped value and how many dialogs fell in
it. A null in the data becomes the literal `(none)` rather than being
dropped, so the buckets sum to the total.

count.description: How many dialogs fell in this bucket.

value.description: The grouped value, rendered as a string.

BucketDeltaView.description: One value's movement between the two captures. `value` is raw.

a.description: Dialogs in this bucket in capture `a`.

b.description: Dialogs in this bucket in capture `b`.

delta.description: `b - a`. Negative means the value became rarer.

value.description: The grouped value, raw. Absent from a side means zero there.

CallReport.description: Serialized form of DialogJson (src/output/json.rs): the `--call-report --json` output and GET /v1/dialogs/{id}. The embedded `streams` items mirror stream.schema.json (kept self-contained, no cross-file $ref).

frame.description: Pointer to the frame this dialog opened in, as `<source>#<ordinal>@<digest>`. Follow it with `sipnab --show-frame`, which checks the digest and refuses when the capture changed since the pointer was made. Optional, and absent rather than null when the dialog has no frame (live capture): absent means unknown, and a value that is present is always a real pointer.

input_origin.description: Which capture source delivered the message that OPENED this dialog. First, never latest: one process can capture from an interface and a HEP mirror at once, and with no BPF filter excluding the mirrored signaling ports the same message arrives from both, so a field reassigned per message would report whichever spoke last. Absent rather than null when the opening message came from no captured packet.

siprec.description: Recording metadata, when this call carried SIPREC (RFC 7866). Omitted, never null, on a call that is not recorded. Declared here because `additionalProperties` is false: it has been emitted since 0.5.x and was never in this schema, so every consumer validating sipnab's output rejected the report of a recorded call outright.

mode.description: Recording mode from the metadata, e.g. `complete`. Optional, and absent rather than null when the metadata named none.

participants.description: Participants the recording metadata describes. Present and possibly empty, never absent, on a recorded call.

name.description: Display name of the participant, as the metadata wrote it.

participant_id.description: Participant identifier from the metadata XML.

session_id.description: Recording session identifier from the SIPREC metadata XML. Optional, and absent rather than null when the metadata named none.

streams.description: Media streams the recording metadata describes. Present and possibly empty, never absent, on a recorded call.

label.description: SDP label associating the stream with an `m=` line. The load-bearing field: SIPREC describes what was recorded, and the label is the only route from a recorded stream back to both its media description and the participant who owns it.

participant_id.description: The participant this stream belongs to.

stream_id.description: Stream identifier from the metadata XML.

termination.description: Why the call ended, when anything on the wire said so. Read from the LAST message naming a cause — `Reason` on a `BYE` or a `CANCEL` counts, which is the case this exists for: a call that clears normally has no failure response to hang a cause on. NOT a diagnosis: a `BYE` carrying `Reason: Q.850;cause=16` is a healthy call clearing normally, so this sits beside the verdict rather than among the fault detections. Optional, and absent rather than null when nothing named a cause.

cause_code.description: The cause number, on the scale `protocol` names. Absent rather than zero when the message named a protocol and no cause, because 0 is itself a real Q.850 cause and a reader could not tell a default from a measurement.

cause_text.description: The human-readable cause, control characters stripped and bounded to `MAX_CAUSE_TEXT_CHARS` (200) characters. Written by whoever sent the message.

frame_ref.description: Index into the dialog's message list of the message that carried the cause.

protocol.description: Which scale `cause_code` is on — RFC 3326's `protocol`, `Q.850` or `SIP` in practice, kept as the sender spelled it. A code without this is not interpretable: 16 is normal clearing in Q.850 and is not a SIP status code at all.

source_header.description: Which header carried the cause: `Reason` (RFC 3326) or `X-Asterisk-HangupCauseCode`. What a vendor header asserts and what RFC 3326 asserts are not the same claim, and a reader deciding how far to trust the number needs to know which.

CallReport.title: sipnab call report / full dialog (DialogJson)

CallReport_amplitude_span.description: A stretch of audio located within the decoded stream. 'This call had dead air' and 'this call went silent forty seconds in' are different findings.

amplitude.description: What the decoded audio DID, present ONLY when the run retained audio (--retain-audio). Absent means NOT MEASURED and never 'clean': without samples there is nothing to look at, and a consumer reading absence as a pass signs off a silent call. These are amplitude measurements and not a quality score -- a gateway sending full-rate frames of digital silence produces perfect packet statistics, a grounded MOS of 4.36, and a call nobody can hear.

clipping.description: Any measured stream ran at its codec's own full scale for longer than the reported minimum run.

dead_air.description: Any measured stream sat below the floor for longer than the reported minimum.

streams_measured.description: Streams whose audio was decoded. At least one, because the object is absent when none were.

CallReport_icmp_media.description: What ICMP said about this capture's MEDIA. Keyed by the quoted datagram's own 5-tuple, not by Call-ID, because a media datagram carries none — so this is a different question from signaling_diagnosis.icmp_unreachable and the two are never merged. Omitted entirely when the capture drew no ICMP quoting non-SIP traffic. `capture` is capture-wide and travels with every dialog so a reader of one call can see that evidence exists; `findings` holds only the findings whose attribution named THIS dialog.

capture.description: Run-wide outcome counters. Three separate outcomes, never collapsed: attributed + unattributed == errors, and sum(finding.errors) + unkeyed + untracked_flows == errors.

CallReport_icmp_media_finding.description: One quoted flow the network reported as undeliverable.

attribution.description: Which rule tied this flow to tracked media. REQUIRED and enumerated: the five tiers are not equally strong claims — `flow` is an exact directed 5-tuple match, `none` is no match at all — and a consumer that cannot tell them apart would present a guess with the confidence of a measurement. A finding without this field is worse than no finding.

payload.description: What the router quoted, as opposed to what sipnab tied it to. A quote can be unmistakably RTP and match nothing, or match a stream exactly with no payload left to read.

CallReport_signaling_diagnosis.description: Signaling-side diagnosis. Every detection is optional and absent means checked-and-not-detected; the whole object is omitted when nothing fired.

icmp_unreachable.description: An ICMP/ICMPv6 error quoting one of this dialog's requests. Omitted entirely (not null) when absent, because the check can only run on a capture that holds ICMP at all: null would claim it ran. `unreachable_endpoint` is the socket that did not answer; `reported_by` is the router or host that reported it, which is a different address and is not the fault. `truncated` says the quote sipnab read was a prefix of the original datagram, which RFC 792 permits and most routers do.

source_disagreement.description: The run's two capture sources do not tell the same story about this call. A HEP mirror reports what the proxy BELIEVES it did; a local capture reports what actually left the box, so the two are complementary rather than redundant and their disagreement is the finding. Omitted entirely (not null) when absent, because the comparison can only run when BOTH witnesses carried this call: null would claim they were compared and agreed. A call one witness never saw at all is deliberately silent here -- from inside such a call, a proxy that mirrored a phantom cannot be told from a witness that was not watching that call's signaling. A message either capture dropped also looks exactly like one a source never carried, which is why this is a finding to investigate rather than a verdict.

agreed.description: How many messages both witnesses carried -- the denominator that makes the gap counts mean something.

evidence.description: Every message index this finding drew on, sorted and deduplicated.

mirror_only.description: Messages the HEP mirror reported that the wire never carried: a proxy that believes it sent something this capture never saw leave the box.

index.description: Index into this dialog's own message list, the same coordinate every `evidence` array uses.

summary.description: What the message is -- `INVITE`, `200 OK` -- so a report pasted into a ticket says something without the reader joining `index` against a message list they do not have.

sdp_differs.description: Messages both witnesses carried whose SDP named different media endpoints -- a rewrite.

mirror.description: Media endpoints the HEP mirror's copy advertised, `<media> <addr>:<port>` in `m=` order. Empty when that copy carried no SDP at all, which is itself a disagreement.

wire.description: Media endpoints the copy captured on the wire advertised. Reported beside `mirror` and never instead of it: there is no expected/actual pair here, because an SDP rewritten between the proxy's account and the wire is sometimes the SBC doing its job and sometimes the bug.

wire_only.description: Messages the wire carried that the mirror never reported: the box did something its own trace does not admit to.

index.description: Index into this dialog's own message list, the same coordinate every `evidence` array uses.

summary.description: What the message is -- `INVITE`, `200 OK` -- so a report pasted into a ticket says something without the reader joining `index` against a message list they do not have.

dialog_assertion.description: WHO asserted the SDP media endpoint that named this stream's dialog: `signaled` (a negotiating party describing its own address) or `media-relay` (an rtpengine relay describing a port it allocated, learned from its `ng` control plane). A different question from `dialog_origin`, which says which capture SOURCE delivered the assertion. A relay's address is authoritative -- it cannot be wrong about which port it opened -- but it names the leg's MIDPOINT rather than either party's endpoint, so the two answers describe different pictures of where the media went. Emitted whenever it is known, `signaled` included: suppressing the common case would make absence mean both 'a party said so' and 'nobody recorded who said so'. Absent therefore means only the latter.

dialog_origin.description: Which source delivered the SDP that named this stream's dialog, present ONLY when it differs from `input_origin` — the binding crossed capture sources. A cross-source tie is weaker than a same-source one: the SDP says what the proxy believes it did and the media says what the NIC saw, and the two can disagree. Absent means either a same-source binding or one whose sources nobody recorded, never 'they agree'.

dscp.description: DSCP of this stream's FIRST packet (RFC 2474). Absent rather than null when no IP header was observed (a HEP-fed stream), so absent means unknown and 0 means observed best effort.

dscp_last.description: DSCP of this stream's most recent packet, present ONLY when it differs from `dscp` — the stream was re-marked in flight.

frame.description: Pointer to the frame this stream's first packet arrived in, as `<source>#<ordinal>@<digest>`. Follow it with `sipnab --show-frame`, which checks the digest and refuses when the capture changed since the pointer was made. Optional, and absent rather than null when the stream has no frame (live capture): absent means unknown, and a value that is present is always a real pointer.

input_origin.description: Which capture source this stream's MEDIA arrived over. Absent rather than null when the stream came from no captured packet.

CallReport_stream_amplitude.description: One stream's amplitude measurement, with every threshold that produced it. The thresholds are fields and not documentation: a finding whose threshold lives only in the source is a finding nobody can argue with.

clip_threshold.description: The absolute sample magnitude a clip was counted at, derived from full_scale.

dead_air_ms.description: Total dead air, which is not the longest span.

floor_dbfs.description: RMS below this, relative to full_scale, counts as silence.

full_scale.description: The largest magnitude this stream's decoder can produce. NOT 32767 for G.711: mu-law tops out at 32124 and A-law at 32256, so a clip test written against the container's maximum never fires on either.

min_clip_run.description: The shortest run of consecutive clipped samples counted. One sample at the ceiling is a loud sample; a run is a waveform with its top cut off.

min_dead_air_ms.description: The shortest run of silent windows reported. Normal conversation is roughly half silence, so a shorter minimum would report every healthy call.

window_ms.description: The window the RMS was measured over.

CallTree.description: The tree of legs reachable from one call across a B2BUA, SBC or PBX.

first_activity.description: Earliest leg creation time in the tree, RFC 3339.

heuristic_edges.description: How many edges are timing guesses rather than identifier matches.

last_activity.description: Latest leg update time in the tree, RFC 3339.

legs.description: Every leg found, ordered by depth then creation time.

root_call_id.description: Call-ID the walk started from, echoed verbatim.

total_legs.description: Number of legs returned, root included.

total_messages.description: Total SIP messages across every leg.

truncated.description: True when the row cap stopped the walk before it ran out of legs.

CallTreeLeg.description:
One leg of a call tree: a dialog, and how the walk reached it. Follow
`call_id` to `/v1/dialogs/{call_id}` for the leg's detail.

depth.description: Hops from the root. Zero for the root itself.

followed.description:
Whether the walk continued THROUGH this leg. False on a leg reached
by a timing guess, and on any leg the cap cut the walk short of.

identifier_match.description:
Whether the edge compared identifiers rather than guessing. Null for
the root, which the caller named rather than the walk matching.

parent_call_id.description: The leg this one was correlated FROM. Null for the root.

score.description: Confidence of the edge from the parent, 0-100. Null for the root.

strategy.description: Which strategy matched this edge. Null for the root.

Capabilities.description:
What this build can do and what the operator turned on: the machine
contract a client reads before it asks, so a refusal it could have
predicted does not read as a dead end. The build fields are the same the
MCP `server_capabilities` tool returns — one canonical `compiled_features`
list — paired with the REST server's own runtime opt-ins.

can_decrypt.description: True when this build can decrypt TLS.

can_hep.description: True when this build can receive HEP.

can_plugins.description: True when this build can load WASM plugins.

features.description:
Compiled-in feature names, sorted. The canonical `compiled_features`
list, shared with `--version` and the MCP tool so no two surfaces
claim different builds of the same binary.

version.description: The crate version this binary was built from.

CapabilitiesRuntime.description:
The REST server's startup opt-ins, each off by default, so a client can
tell a capability this build lacks from one this run did not turn on.

api_allow_relay_query.description:
Whether this run may transmit a relay query — `--api-allow-relay-query`
on a live source. Off means the `/v1/relay/...` routes answer
`not_configured` or `not_permitted` rather than reaching the relay.

CaptureComparisonView.description: Two capture files diffed by aggregate. Bucket values are raw.

dimensions.description: One entry per requested dimension, in the order requested.

summary.description: What the two sides are and what the numbers do not cover.

CaptureIdentity.description:
Which capture an answer came from, and which revision of its stores.

Compare two of these to learn what changed: a different `instance`
means a different capture, and every cursor, index and Call-ID from the
earlier answer is meaningless; the same instance with a higher
generation means the same capture grew.

The SAME identity MCP's `capture_status` stamps its answers with, from
the same object, so an agent and an HTTP client polling one process can
tell they are describing one capture.

dialog_generation.description: Dialog-store mutations since it was created or cleared.

instance.description: Identifies the loaded capture. Opaque — compare it, never parse it.

node.description:
Which box saw this. Stable for the process; does not rotate with
`instance`.

stream_generation.description: Stream-store mutations since it was created or cleared.

CaptureReport.description:
`GET /v1/report` — the whole-capture analysis.

Serialized from `crate::analysis::CaptureAnalysis` itself, never
re-parsed out of a rendered report: `print_analysis_report_as` looks
like it has a JSON arm and does not, and asking it for JSON is how this
endpoint once returned 500.

complete.description:
Whether the analysis saw the whole capture. `false` means a
retention cap shed something, and every count above is a floor.

findings.description: What the analysis found, across every dialog and stream.

frames_read.description:
Frames the capture read, from the same process-global the
Prometheus scrape reports — so this denominator is the one every
other number in the run is read against.

CaptureSideView.description: What reading one capture produced, for `GET /v1/captures/compare`.

dialogs_dropped.description:
Dialogs the scratch store's capacity refused; non-zero means this
side is truncated and every count is a floor.

read_error.description: Why the read stopped early, when it did.

Comparison.description: Two calls side by side, naming which fields differ.

differences.description:
The field names that differ — a subset of `state`,
`final_status_code`, `msg_count`, `methods`, in that order. Empty
when the two calls match on all four. `hints` is reported per side
but not diffed.

ComparisonSide.description:
One call summarized for a side-by-side comparison: the fields
`/v1/dialogs/compare` diffs, the same the MCP `compare_dialogs` tool
reports.

final_status_code.description: The final INVITE response code, null while the call is in progress.

hints.description: The signaling-diagnosis hints for the call.

methods.description: The distinct request methods seen, sorted.

msg_count.description: How many SIP messages the dialog holds.

Correlated.description: The other legs of one call, with the source it was asked about.

heuristic_only.description:
True when every matched leg is a timing guess rather than an
identifier match, so a reader weighs the whole answer accordingly.

legs.description: The correlated legs, highest score first.

source_call_id.description: The Call-ID the legs were correlated against.

total_matched.description: How many legs matched before the row cap.

CorrelatedLeg.description:
One other leg of a call, and the strategy that matched it. The fields
mirror the MCP `find_correlated` tool's `CorrelatedLeg`, built from the
one `CorrelationResult::strategy_and_gap` rule so the two surfaces cannot
disagree about whether a strategy is an identifier match.

call_id.description: Call-ID of the correlated dialog. Feed it to `/v1/dialogs/{call_id}`.

identifier_match.description: True when the strategy compared identifiers, false for a guess.

observed_gap_ms.description:
For `timing_heuristic` only: the observed gap between the two
dialogs' creation, in milliseconds. Null for an identifier match,
where it would be a number with no bearing on why they matched.

strategy.description:
Which strategy matched, by name: `session_id`, `x_call_id`,
`sdp_origin`, `charging_vector_related_icid`, `charging_vector_icid`,
`via_branch` or `timing_heuristic`.

Dialog.description:
`GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}` — the full dialog.

The projection `output::json::dialog_to_json` builds, which is a
SUPERSET of [`DialogSummary`] and not the same shape: it carries the
display names, the SDP timeline, the media diagnosis and the streams
themselves. `tests/openapi_contract_test.rs` reads a real one off a
running server and fails if a key here is missing from it, or one of
its keys is missing from here.

The nested objects are left open rather than enumerated. Their
definitions live in `output::json`, and repeating them here would be
the drift this document exists to remove; the live check is what holds
the top level honest.

diagnosis.description:
The media diagnosis: three booleans plus `hints`. There is no
`summary` member.

final_status_code.description: Final INVITE response code, once the call reached one.

frame.description: `<source>#<ordinal>` pointer to the frame this dialog opened in.

from.description: User part of the From URI.

from_display.description: Display name from the From header.

icmp_media.description: ICMP evidence bearing on the media, when any was seen.

input_origin.description: Capture source that delivered the opening message.

method.description: SIP method that opened the dialog.

sdp_timeline.description: Every SDP offer and answer, in order.

signaling_diagnosis.description: The signaling diagnosis, when one could be made.

streams.description: The RTP streams this dialog claims.

tags.description:
Labels the analysis attached to this dialog. Absent, not empty,
when it attached none.

timing.description:
Transaction timing, with the ring and teardown legs the summary
omits.

to.description: User part of the To URI.

to_display.description: Display name from the To header.

by_method.description:
What `total` is made of, split by the method that opened each
dialog and ordered dominant-first.

Over the filtered set, not over this page: a breakdown of the page
would describe the page. A dialog list is dominated by whatever the
deployment does most, which in the field is usually the keepalive
plane rather than the calls, and without this a client cannot tell
that from the rows it was handed.

limit.description: The `limit` actually applied, after clamping to `--api-max-rows`.

offset.description: The `offset` this page was taken at.

total.description:
Size of the FILTERED result set — the count the rows are drawn
from, so paging by `total` terminates.

DialogSummary.description:
One row of `GET /v1/dialogs`.

Marker only: the component is spliced from
`tests/schemas/dialog.schema.json`, which
`tests/openapi_contract_test.rs` also checks against this declaration,
so the two cannot disagree about a property name.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the first message.

duration_sec.description: First to last message, seconds. `0` for a single-message dialog.

final_status_code.description:
Final INVITE response code, once the call reached one. Absent —
never zero — while the call is still in progress.

frame.description: `<source>#<ordinal>` pointer to the frame this dialog opened in.

from_user.description: User part of the From URI.

input_origin.description:
Which capture source delivered the opening message — `wire`, `hep`
or `uprobe`.

method.description: SIP method that opened the dialog, canonical form.

to_user.description: User part of the To URI.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent message.

distinct_values.description: Distinct values seen across both captures.

EndpointBannerRow.description: A `User-Agent` or `Server` banner an endpoint sent, and how often.

header.description:
The header that carried it — `User-Agent` on a request, `Server` on
a response.

value.description: The banner text, as the sender wrote it (raw, unfenced).

by_final_status.description: Count per final INVITE status code.

failed.description: Of those, how many ended 4xx, 5xx or 6xx.

failure_rate_pct.description:
`failed` over `with_final_status`, as a percent. Null when nothing
has reached a final status.

with_final_status.description: Of those, how many reached a final INVITE response.

EndpointDescription.description:
Everything one endpoint did, selected by ip or user. The same facets the
MCP `describe_endpoint` tool reports, minus its security findings — those
are the separate security-findings capability, not this route.

contact_rewrite.description:
Whether a private `Contact` this endpoint registered was rewritten.
Null when the endpoint sent no REGISTER.

dialogs.description: Dialogs the endpoint took part in.

messages_received.description: Messages addressed TO the endpoint (zero for a user lookup).

messages_sent.description: Messages the endpoint SENT (zero for a user lookup).

recent_dialogs.description: The most recent dialogs, newest first, bounded by `limit`.

stack.description: The signaling stack fingerprint, read off request syntax.

user_agents.description: Banners the endpoint sent, most frequent first, raw.

applicable.description: False when the endpoint sent no REGISTER at all.

auth_loops.description: Of those, how many are looping on authentication.

failed.description: Of those, how many the diagnosis calls a registration failure.

problem_call_ids.description: Call-IDs of the REGISTER dialogs that failed or looped.

succeeded.description: Of those, how many drew a 2xx.

EndpointStreamsView.description: RTP an endpoint sent or received. Codecs are raw.

lost_packets.description: Total packets the sequence gaps say were lost.

max_jitter_ms.description: Worst interarrival jitter seen on any of them, milliseconds.

orphaned.description: Of those, how many are not linked to any dialog.

HepRefusedSourceRow.description:
One address the listener has been turning away.

Keyed by address alone, never by the capture id a refused packet claimed:
a packet that failed authentication has proven nothing, including its id.

by_reason.description: Those packets by reason, only the reasons that occurred.

first_seen.description: When the first of them arrived (RFC 3339, UTC).

last_seen.description: When the latest of them arrived (RFC 3339, UTC).

packets.description: Packets refused from it while it has been in the table.

peer.description: The address the refused packets came from.

HepSenderRow.description: One sender feeding a HEP listener.

capture_id.description: The capture-agent id the sender claims, when its packets carry one.

first_seen.description: When its first admitted packet arrived (RFC 3339, UTC).

identity.description:
Always `claimed_by_sender`: the id is what the sender says, and no
certificate or per-sender key proves it.

last_seen.description: When its latest admitted packet arrived (RFC 3339, UTC).

peer.description: The address its packets came from.

silent.description:
Whether it has been silent for at least the threshold. "Silent", not
"down": a PBX with no calls at night may legitimately send nothing.

source.description:
The source half of every frame pointer this sender's packets carry
(`hep:<capture-id>@<peer>`), so a row and a pointer name one sender
the same way.

trust.description: The trust the listener admitted it under.

HepSendersReport.description:
Who is feeding a HEP listener, who stopped, and who it is turning away.

ONE shape for every surface that answers the question: `--hep-senders` at
the end of a run, `GET /v1/hep/senders`, the MCP `hep_senders` tool and the
TUI's HEP senders view all serialize or render this struct, built by
[`crate::capture::hep_roster::RosterState::report`]. A second shape would
be a second answer, and REST and MCP must return the same bytes for one
roster.

# What the identity is, and is not

Every sender is keyed by the capture-agent id it CLAIMS (HEP chunk
`0x000c`) and the address its packets came from. Neither is proven: one
shared secret serves the whole listener, so any sender holding it can
claim any id, and no client certificate is asked for. Each row says so in
`identity`, rather than a reader inferring a proof that was never made.

# What it holds

Counters, addresses, ids and times. No byte of any packet, so it needs no
fencing on the MCP surface for the reason `runtime_stats` needs none.

listening.description:
Whether this run has a HEP listener at all. `false` is a run with no
`-L`/`--hep-listen`, and every count below is then zero because
nothing was listening, not because nothing was sent.

note.description: Why every count is zero, when the run has no HEP listener.

packets_received.description: Every packet the listener received, admitted or refused.

refused_by_reason.description:
Refused packets by reason, every reason present, zeros included, so a
reader can tell "never happened" from "not reported".

refused_sources.description:
The refused sources, most refused first, at most the row limit the
caller asked for.

refused_sources_evicted.description:
Addresses evicted from that table to make room. Their refusals still
count in `refused_by_reason`, which nothing evicts.

refused_sources_limit.description:
The most addresses that table will hold. It evicts the address refused
least recently, so a spoofed flood rotates it rather than freezing it.

refused_sources_tracked.description: Distinct addresses the refused-source table holds now.

senders.description:
The tracked senders, by peer address and then capture id, at most the
row limit the caller asked for.

senders_limit.description:
The most senders it will track (`[limits] max_tracked_peers`). Past it
a new sender is still admitted, but is neither listed nor numbered.

senders_silent.description: Tracked senders silent for at least the threshold.

senders_tracked.description: Senders the listener is tracking, whether or not all are listed below.

silence_threshold_seconds.description:
Seconds without an admitted packet before a sender, or the whole
listener, is reported silent (`--hep-silence-warn`). `0` means the
warning is off, and no sender is ever reported silent.

trust.description:
The trust the listener admits packets under: `unauthenticated`,
`shared_secret_plain` or `shared_secret_hmac`. Absent when not
listening.

untracked_packets.description:
Packets admitted from senders that arrived after the tracking table
was full. Counted rather than dropped from the account: the table
refuses new entries instead of recycling old ones, so these are the
traffic the rows below cannot show.

Lint.description: The RFC-conformance findings for one dialog.

call_id.description: The Call-ID the findings are for.

finding_count.description: How many findings the dialog tripped.

findings.description: The findings, in the linter's own order.

LintFinding.description:
One RFC-conformance finding: the rule, its severity and basis, the RFC
section it reads from, and what the message held against what the section
calls for. The same fields the MCP `lint_dialog` tool reports.

basis.description:
What kind of claim the rule makes: `must`, `should`, `interop` or
`observation`. A `must` violation and an interop wart are not the
same finding, and the word keeps them apart.

expected.description: What the cited section calls for.

explanation.description: Why the difference matters, in the terms an operator acts on.

message_index.description:
Index into the dialog's messages of the message the finding is drawn
from.

rfc.description: RFC number the rule reads from.

severity.description: How loudly to report it: `error`, `warning` or `info`.

MethodCount.description:
One opening method and how many dialogs in the filtered set it opened.

A list of pairs rather than an object: JSON object key order is not
guaranteed, and the useful reading of this field is "what dominates",
which only an ordered sequence can carry.

count.description: How many dialogs in the filtered set it opened.

method.description:
The method that opened the dialogs — `INVITE`, `REGISTER`, and so
on.

PersistenceRequest.description:
The body `POST /v1/persistence` accepts.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a caller who misspells the key is told, rather
than getting a 200 that moved nothing. The field is required and typed:
serde refuses a string, a number, and a missing key alike, and every one of
those refusals leaves the gate where it was.

enabled.description: What the caller wants the gate to be, narrowed by the command line.

PersistenceState.description: The body both doors of `/v1/persistence` answer with.

authorized.description:
The command line's ceiling. A caller that asked to enable an
unauthorized run reads `enabled: false, authorized: false` rather
than a bare 200 it would take for success.

enabled.description: Whether content may reach disk on this run right now.

Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body: what every 4xx and 5xx
carries.

Serialized by [`super::Problem`]'s `IntoResponse`, so this is the wire
type itself rather than a description of one.

detail.description: What went wrong THIS time. Absent when the kind says it all.

status.description:
The HTTP status, repeated so the body survives being logged apart
from its response.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of that kind.

type.description: URI naming the problem KIND. The field a client branches on.

RateGroup.description:
One group's carrier metrics, with the population behind them and the
reason for any metric its population could not support.

count.description:
Dialogs in the group (the same as `population.dialogs`, surfaced for
a reader who reads only the top line).

metrics.description:
Each requested metric to its value, or null when the population could
not support it — the reason is then in `not_grounded`.

not_grounded.description:
For each null metric, the population that was missing. A null with no
entry here would be a silent gap.

population.description: The populations every figure was computed over.

value.description: The dimension value this group is keyed on.

RatePopulation.description:
The populations one rate group's figures were computed over, published so
a reader checks every ratio against its denominator.

completed_calls.description: Calls both answered and torn down inside the capture (the ACD base).

delivered.description: Seizures the far end decided (answered or an E.411 destination code).

mos_grounded_dialogs.description: Dialogs a grounded MOS was scored for.

pdd_measured.description: Dialogs a post-dial delay was measured for.

retransmits.description: Retransmitted messages summed across the group.

seizures.description: INVITE dialogs that reached a final response.

Rates.description: Carrier metrics per group over the dialog store, one dimension.

distinct_values.description: How many distinct values the dimension took, before the cut.

group_by.description: The dimension the metrics were grouped by, echoed verbatim.

groups.description: The groups, largest first, ties broken by value for a stable answer.

other_count.description:
Dialogs in every group past the `top_n` cut, so the groups plus this
account for `total_matched`.

total_matched.description: How many dialogs the filter admitted, across all groups.

units.description: Each metric name to the unit it is expressed in.

RelayStatsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/relay/...` — one envelope for every relay route (ST5): the four
statistics routes and the two holdings routes.

`outcome` is always present: `ok` for a clean answer, or one of the five
ST-S4 classifications. Every other field is optional because the shape
depends on which route answered and whether it was clean -- a client
branches on `outcome` first. Deliberately permissive (the payload
sub-objects are open) because one envelope carries several different clean
shapes plus the classifications, and pinning each would be a schema per
route where the discriminator already tells them apart.

call_id.description: The Call-ID asked about (holdings per-call route).

call_ids.description: The Call-IDs the relay is holding (holdings list route).

detail.description: A sentence explaining a non-`ok` outcome.

origin.description: `asked` on these routes (a poll is CLI-only and never appears here).

packets.description: The relay-vs-capture comparison (C4): both tiers, a verdict, a note.

refusals.description: Statistics the relay refused, with its own code, listed apart.

relay.description: The relay and where it was asked, on any answer that reached it.

responsibility.description:
Whose problem a non-`ok` outcome is: `invocation` / `relay_or_network`
/ `request` / `answer`.

source.description: How the name list was determined: `listed` or `probed` (C3).

statistics.description: The relay's counters (C1/C2), each with its tier.

tags.description: The tags, ports and streams the relay holds for one call (per-call).

truncated.description: Whether the relay held more Call-IDs than it returned (holdings list).

RtpStream.description: Serialized form of StreamJson (src/output/json.rs); also embedded in a dialog/call-report `streams` array and returned by GET /v1/streams/{id}.

dialog_assertion.description: WHO asserted the SDP media endpoint that named this stream's dialog: `signaled` (a negotiating party describing its own address) or `media-relay` (an rtpengine relay describing a port it allocated, learned from its `ng` control plane). A different question from `dialog_origin`, which says which capture SOURCE delivered the assertion. A relay's address is authoritative -- it cannot be wrong about which port it opened -- but it names the leg's MIDPOINT rather than either party's endpoint, so the two answers describe different pictures of where the media went. Emitted whenever it is known, `signaled` included: suppressing the common case would make absence mean both 'a party said so' and 'nobody recorded who said so'. Absent therefore means only the latter.

dialog_origin.description: Which source delivered the SDP that named this stream's dialog, present ONLY when it differs from `input_origin` — the binding crossed capture sources. A cross-source tie is weaker than a same-source one: the SDP says what the proxy believes it did and the media says what the NIC saw, and the two can disagree. Absent means either a same-source binding or one whose sources nobody recorded, never 'they agree'.

dscp.description: DSCP of this stream's FIRST packet (RFC 2474), the queue the network was asked to put the media in. Voice is conventionally EF (46); 0 is the default PHB and means the media competes with bulk traffic. Optional, and absent rather than null when no IP header was observed (a HEP-fed stream) — so an absent key means the marking is unknown and 0 means it was observed and is best effort.

dscp_last.description: DSCP of this stream's most recent packet, present ONLY when it differs from `dscp` — a stream re-marked in flight, typically at a policy boundary. Its presence is the finding; a steady stream omits it.

frame.description: Pointer to the frame this stream's first packet arrived in, as `<source>#<ordinal>@<digest>` — feed it to `sipnab --show-frame` to retrieve the bytes, which either returns the frame or refuses because the capture changed. The media analogue of the dialog and message `frame`, and the only way to check an ORPHANED stream, which has no Call-ID to look a dialog up by. Optional, and absent rather than null when the stream has no frame (live capture). Not in `required` for that reason: an absent key means unknown, and a present one is always a real pointer.

input_origin.description: Which capture source this stream's MEDIA arrived over. Absent rather than null when the stream came from no captured packet.

RtpStream.title: sipnab RTP stream (StreamJson)

mos.description: MOS for THIS interval alone, scored on the interval's own jitter and loss and on the stream's resolved one-way path delay. The stream-level figure is a mean over the whole call and hides a burst shorter than itself. Read `verdict` before comparing it: on a codec with no impairment value this is a placeholder standing in for a missing measurement, byte-identical to a grounded score.

mos_grounded.description: Whether `mos` and `r_factor` rest on a real impairment value. False exactly when `verdict` is `not_scorable`.

r_factor.description: The ITU-T G.107 R-factor `mos` was converted from, on the same inputs. R is the linear scale carriers write SLAs in, so the eight R-points behind a 0.15 MOS difference are a real difference where the MOS gap reads as rounding.

verdict.description: Three states, not two. `acceptable` is R at or above 70, where ITU-T G.107's worst user-satisfaction category is still 'some users dissatisfied'; `degraded` is below it. `not_scorable` is the ONLY answer for a codec with no published or declared impairment value, and it is not a shade of good or bad: banding a placeholder would paint a guess.

capture_backpressure_blocks_total.description:
Times the capture path blocked on a full queue. Absent for the
reason above.

capture_packets_total.description: Packets the capture path has seen.

capture_queue_depth_packets.description:
Packets waiting in the capture queue. Absent when this run owns no
capture meter — never zero, which would read as a clear queue.

host.description: The host, or the cgroup when sipnab runs inside one.

oneOf.description:
Rates across the sampled window. Present only when the caller sent
`sample_seconds`.

uptime_seconds.description: Seconds this process has been serving.

RuntimeHost.description: The host's totals, or the cgroup's limits inside a container.

basis.description:
Which denominator the figures came from: `host` or `cgroup`.

Named rather than assumed. A percentage against the machine's total
is wrong by a large factor inside a container with a small limit.

RuntimeImpact.description: sipnab's share of the host, and whether that share is load-bearing.

memory_pct.description: Resident set as a percentage of the host total.

note.description: Why, including the threshold and the basis.

significant.description: Whether sipnab is a load-bearing consumer right now.

RuntimeInterface.description:
What an interface reports about itself, as distinct from what sipnab's
capture handle saw.

rx_missed_errors.description: Packets missed because the NIC could not keep up.

speed_mbps.description: Negotiated speed, Mbit/s. Absent on a virtual interface.

RuntimeOccupancy.description: A store's occupancy against the cap it evicts at.

pct.description: `used` over `capacity`, absent when the cap is zero.

RuntimeProcess.description:
sipnab's own process, from `/proc/self`.

Every field is optional: absent means "not readable on this platform",
which is a different fact from zero and must not be rendered as one.

RuntimeRates.description: Rates measured across a sampling window.

calls_per_second.description: Dialogs opened per second across the window.

calls_per_second_by_method.description:
Dialogs opened per second, split by the method that opened them,
most-opened first. `[["OPTIONS", 2.8], ["INVITE", 0.6]]`.

packets_per_second.description: Packets per second across the window.

window_seconds.description: The window actually sampled, seconds — not the one requested.

SecurityFinding.description: One security finding an armed detector recorded. The `detail` is raw.

detail.description: The detector's own detail line, raw (the MCP surface fences it).

src_ip.description: The source address the finding is about.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the finding fired.

SecurityFindings.description: The armed detectors' recorded findings, with the armed-state distinction.

armed_kinds.description:
The detectors armed on this server, by the rule name each files
under. Empty means nothing is armed.

detection_armed.description:
True when at least one detector is armed. An empty `findings` with
this false means nothing was watching, NOT that traffic was clean.

findings.description: This page of findings, newest first, raw.

note.description: Present only when nothing is armed, saying so in words.

returned.description: Rows in `findings`, so counting the array is never necessary.

total_matched.description:
Findings matching the filter across the whole retained ring,
independent of `limit`.

truncated.description:
True when matches remain after this page. Narrow with `since` or
raise `limit`.

SkippedPort.description: One of the busiest ports the port gate excluded.

messages.description: SIP messages seen on it and set aside.

oneOf.description:
WHICH capture these counts came from, and which revision of its
stores. `null` when nobody told this server what it is attached to.

capture_name.description: Human name of the capture, when one is known.

capture_quality.description: How much of the wire the counts above are drawn from.

caveats.description:
What this capture DECLINED to do, beside what it lost. Always
present and always complete: zero is a real answer, and a key that
shows up only on a bad run is a key no client learns exists.

source.description: What the server is attached to. `unknown` is a real answer.

source_exhausted.description: Whether a file source has been read to the end.

unanalysed_busiest_ports.description:
The five busiest ports behind `unanalysed_sip_messages`. Widen
`--portrange` to recover them.

unanalysed_sip_messages.description: SIP messages the port gate excluded before anything analyzed them.

unsaved.description:
True only for a LIVE capture with no output file: packets held in
memory and nowhere else.

writing_to.description: Path this capture is writing to, when it is writing.

StatsCaptureQuality.description:
How much of the wire every other count in `GET /v1/stats` is drawn
from.

Without it a total reads as a total when it may be a floor.

degraded.description: Whether any of the above is non-zero.

invalid_timestamps.description: Frames carrying a timestamp that could not be believed.

kernel_dropped_packets.description: Packets the kernel dropped before sipnab saw them.

lapsed_turn_allocation_streams.description: Streams affected by a lapsed TURN allocation.

snapped_frames.description: Frames truncated by the capture snap length.

unanswered_nat_requests.description: NAT-keepalive requests that never drew a response.

undecodable_frames.description: Frames sipnab could not decode at all.

active.description:
Dialogs in an active state. Six states, two of them SUBSCRIBE
dialogs carrying no media — not a count of calls.

StatsTiming.description:
Post-dial-delay percentiles from `GET /v1/stats`.

Every member is `null` when no dialog has a PDD — an absent
measurement, not a zero one.

offset.description: The `offset` this page was taken at.

total.description: Size of the FILTERED result set.

ungrounded_excluded.description:
Streams a `mos_below` bound skipped for want of a grounded score.
Always `0` when `mos_below` is absent, because nothing was bounded.

amr_mode_kbps.description:
The single AMR or AMR-WB mode, kbit/s, that every readable frame of
this stream was coded at. Absent when the sender switched mode, and
absent when the payloads could not be read at all.

amr_modes_observed.description:
How many DISTINCT AMR speech modes the payloads carried. Absent,
never zero, when none were read — so a present value always means
sipnab read the wire.

associated_dialog.description: Call-ID of the dialog that does claim it.

codec.description: Payload codec, when one was identified.

dialog_assertion.description:
WHO asserted the SDP media endpoint that named the dialog:
`signaled` or `media-relay`.

Missing from this document until 0.5.161 while the response
carried it, because nothing compares this schema against the model
it describes — see the backlog's DUP section.

dialog_origin.description: Capture source that delivered the owning dialog.

frame.description: `<source>#<ordinal>` pointer to the first frame of the stream.

input_origin.description: Capture source that delivered the first packet.

loss_pct.description: Loss as a percentage of expected packets.

mos.description: Estimated MOS. Read `mos_grounded` before comparing it.

mos_grounded.description:
Whether `mos` is a measurement or a placeholder standing in for a
codec with no published impairment value. `?mos_below=` admits only
grounded scores.

mos_note.description: Caveat attached to this particular score.

packets.description: RTP packets counted on this stream.

r_factor.description:
The E-model R-factor the MOS was converted from, same delay basis
and same grounding caveat. An SLA is written in R, and R is the
linear scale.

round_trip_ms.description: Round-trip time, milliseconds, when one could be measured.

round_trip_source.description: What the round trip was measured from.

TailPage.description:
A page of dialogs updated since a cursor, for change-tracking pollers.
Doc-only, like [`DialogList`]: the route answers with the same untyped
summaries `/v1/dialogs` builds, so this mirrors the shape for the
contract test rather than being serialized directly.

dialogs.description:
The dialogs updated strictly after the request cursor, oldest update
first, ties broken by Call-ID.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque cursor (`<RFC 3339>|<Call-ID>` of the last row) to pass back
as `since` to resume. Null when no dialogs matched.

Talker.description:
One ranked talker: a participant and what it did across the dialogs it
took part in. The same fields the MCP `top_talkers` tool reports.

answered.description: Of `invites`, the ones that reached a 2xx.

failed.description: Of `invites`, the ones that ended 4xx, 5xx or 6xx.

key.description:
The talker's key — an address (`ip`), a banner (`ua`), or the dialed
number's leading digits (`prefix`).

share_pct.description:
The share of matched dialogs this talker appeared in, as a percent.
Null on an empty capture, where a zero would read as a talker
measured to be idle. Shares sum above 100% because a dialog counts
for every participant.

Talkers.description: The busiest participants, ranked largest first.

by.description: The dimension ranked by (`ip`, `ua` or `prefix`), echoed verbatim.

distinct_talkers.description: How many distinct talkers the filter admitted, before the page cut.

talkers.description: The ranked talkers, busiest first, ties broken by messages then key.

total_matched.description: How many dialogs the filter admitted, the share denominator.

truncated.description: True when there are more distinct talkers than the page returned.

TfpsAction.description:
`tfps_ctl ban --json`, `unban --json`, and every line `ingest` answers
with: what TFPS did about one address.

applied.description: Whether the firewall was written. False for a refusal and a dry run.

expires.description:
When the block lapses, epoch seconds; `null` for never, for an unban,
and for anything refused.

ip.description: The address, or `null` when the input did not name a valid one.

refused.description:
Why not, in TFPS's own vocabulary: `local` (an address of the host
itself), `declared` (an operator `ignoreip` entry), `kernel` (the map
write failed -- enforcement is broken, not policy), `not-blocked` for
an unban that found nothing. `null` when it was applied.

source.description: Who asked: `operator` for the two commands, `sipnab` for `ingest`.

oneOf.description: What TFPS did, when it was asked -- a refusal included.

installed.description: Whether a `tfps_ctl` was found to ask.

tfps_ctl.description: The executable that answered, when one did.

TfpsBanRequest.description:
The body `POST /v1/tfps/ban` accepts.

`deny_unknown_fields` for the reason `PersistenceRequest` gives: a caller
who misspells `ttl_secs` is told, rather than getting a ban of the wrong
duration.

ip.description: The source to condemn, an IPv4 address (TFPS's block map is IPv4).

ttl_secs.description:
How long the ban lasts, in seconds; `0` is forever. Absent takes
TFPS's default of an hour. TFPS's `ban` takes no reason.

detail.description:
What the reason saw. For `user-agent` this is the sender's own text.
`null` when unknown.

enforced.description: Whether the firewall holds it, or TFPS is only observing.

expires.description: When it lapses, epoch seconds; `null` for a ban that does not.

first_seen.description: When the ban began, epoch seconds; `null` when unknown.

reason.description:
Why it was condemned, in TFPS's own vocabulary -- the `block_log`
column, the `REASON` its human view prints. `apiban` with detail
`feed` when the address came from the feed rather than the perimeter;
`null` when the block predates the audit row that would say.

events.description: Events TFPS recorded for the source.

ip.description: The source whose packets were dropped.

last_request.description:
The last request line the source sent -- the sender's own text;
`null` when none was recorded.

rule.description: The rule behind the block; `null` when unknown.

TfpsLabel.description:
One row of `tfps_ctl log --json`: a verdict about one source.

The same shape `tests/fixtures/tfps-labels-golden.jsonl` pins for the
label harness, which reads it structurally rather than through this type
for the reason its header gives.

disposition.description:
What TFPS did about it, from `CONTEXT.md`'s disposition vocabulary:
`ignore`, `exempt`, `would-block`, `block`. A released TFPS only ever
writes `block`, because `block_log` has no column for the rest.

expires.description:
Unix seconds when a block lapses; `0` for never; `null` when nothing
was blocked.

first_seen.description: Unix seconds when the verdict was reached.

ip.description: The source the disposition is about.

reason.description:
Why it was reached, in TFPS's own vocabulary -- the `block_log`
column, the `REASON` its human view prints.

unbanned_at.description: Unix seconds when an operator lifted the block, when one did.

installed.description: Whether a `tfps_ctl` was found to ask.

rows.description: The rows, at most the door's row cap of them.

What the reason saw. For `user-agent` this is the sender's own text.

tfps_ctl.description: The executable that answered, when one did.

Rows the peer returned before the cap. For `tfps_labels` that is at

items.description:
One row of `tfps_ctl log --json`: a verdict about one source.

`ignore`, `exempt`, `would-block`, `block`. A released TFPS only ever
writes `block`, because `block_log` has no column for the rest.

enforcement.description:
`active` when bans reach the firewall, `inactive` when no block map
could be opened -- and the reason for that goes to TFPS's stderr.

interface.description: The interface enforcement applies to; `null` when unknown.

last_checkpoint.description:
Epoch seconds of the newest learned row, so a reader can judge how
stale the snapshot is; `null` before the first checkpoint.

map.description:
Which enforcement plane TFPS is editing, in its own words -- `own map
id 59`, `pinned map <path>`, `shared map <path>`. `null` when no map
could be opened. This is the one enforcement fact `tfps_ctl` can see
for itself: it opens the block map, not the XDP program, which is why

mode.description:
How the firewall is driven, in TFPS's vocabulary (`native`, ...);
`null` when it could not look.

pairs.description:
Learned pairs at the last checkpoint; `null` when the database could
not be read. Equal to `peers` on a released TFPS -- `Store::totals`
counts one column twice -- so do not read them as two facts.

peers.description:
Learned peers at the last checkpoint; `null` when unreadable. See
`pairs`.

TfpsStatusAnswer.description:
`tfps_status`'s answer, on every surface.

One type, serialized by the MCP tool and the REST route alike, so the two
doors cannot drift apart. `installed: false` carries `reason` and nothing
else; `installed: true` carries which executable answered and its answer.

installed.description: Whether a `tfps_ctl` was found to ask.

oneOf.description: What it said, when it did.

tfps_ctl.description: The executable that answered, when one did.

Timeline.description: Call volume over time, in fixed-width buckets.

bucket_seconds.description:
The bucket width actually used, echoed because the caller may have
omitted it.

buckets.description:
One row per interval, oldest first, gaps included (an empty interval
is the outage, so it is not dropped).

TimelineBucket.description: One interval of a call-volume histogram.

bucket_seconds.description: Width of the interval in seconds, echoed so a row reads on its own.

dialogs.description: Dialogs whose first message fell in this interval.

start.description:
Start of the interval, inclusive, RFC 3339. Aligned to the epoch, not
to the first call, so two captures line up.

TimingSummary.description: Transaction timing, as carried by every dialog summary.

duration_ms.description: Answer to BYE, milliseconds. Absent for unanswered or live calls.

`GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/vcon` — one observed dialog as an unsigned
OBSERVER vCon container (draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core).

The container is serialized as a JSON OBJECT, not as `Vcon::to_json`'s
string — a client must not have to parse JSON out of JSON.

`tests/schemas/vcon.schema.json` is the working group's schema and is
deliberately NOT reproduced here: it is theirs, it is draft-07, and its
own text rejects a container shape the working group agreed to at IETF
124. This describes what sipnab sends.

info.description:
Read-only HTTP access to the dialogs, RTP streams, analysis and Prometheus metrics of a running sipnab capture, plus three writes: closing the persistence gate, and relaying an operator's ban or release to the toll-fraud prevention peer when one is installed.

The server reads the same in-memory stores as the capture pipeline, in the same process. There is no database and no history: every answer describes the capture as it stands.
info.title: sipnab REST API

get.description:
Answers 200 with the literal body `ok`, whatever else is wrong.

Deliberately outside the guard: no credential, no rate limit, and no store access. A liveness probe that a rate limit could starve is a probe that reports an outage it caused, and one that reads the stores answers slowly on the capture that most needs watching.

get.description:
Diffs two capture files in `--api-file-root` by aggregate: per dimension, how many dialogs fell in each bucket in each capture and how far that moved, ranked so 'today is worse than yesterday, and here is where' is the first row. The poll a monitoring system makes; the same diff the MCP `compare_captures` tool answers.

Each name is a bare FILENAME, never a path — a separator, a `..`, or a symlink out of the root is refused. Neither file becomes the capture this server serves. Bucket values come back raw, the values a program keys on. The route answers 503 until the server is started with `--api-file-root`, a file-reading capability that is off by default.

Capture held against the baseline: a bare filename in the same root.

(`state`, `response_code`, `method`, `from.user`, `to.user`, `ua`,

Two calls side by side — state, outcome code, message count and method set — with the fields that differ named for you. The same comparison the MCP `compare_dialogs` tool answers.

A client could fetch both dialogs and diff them, but one asked to spot the difference itself will sometimes report a difference that is not there. A Call-ID with no dialog is a 404 that names which of the two is missing.

Every figure carries the population it was computed over, and a metric its population cannot support comes back null with the reason in `not_grounded` rather than as a zero: an ASR of zero over a group of registrations is not a failing trunk. Groups are largest-first by dialog count, and `other_count` carries everything past `top_n`. Beyond the count dimensions this route also groups by `to_domain`, `hour` and `next_hop`.

outside that set is a 400. Required.

sipnab must have retained the payload (`--retain-audio`) for there to be anything to decode. A dialog that carries only undecodable codecs, or whose payload this run did not keep, is a 422 whose body explains which — never a silent empty file. The audio is bounded by where the capture point sat and by what retention kept; it is not a recording the endpoints made.
